headline: Upgrading Leaky or Outdated Fixtures: What to Confirm Before Buying New Hardware
articleBody:
Overview
Swapping out outdated faucets, shower valves, and toilets elevates everyday function while giving your space a clean look. Ensuring mechanical compatibility before buying is the secret to a smooth upgrade.

Key Benefits
Modern plumbing fixtures offer superior ceramic disc valving, durable finishes, and water-conserving performance. Upgrading to WaterSense-labeled models keeps municipal water usage low without sacrificing flow pressure.

Process Breakdown
We check current valve depths, measure rough-in dimensions, and inspect shutoff valves and supply lines. Once the water is safely isolated, we remove old hardware, check drain flanges and subflooring, install the new assembly, and test every joint under full line pressure.

Real Examples
Homeowners often purchase widespread sink faucets only to find their existing vanity countertop is pre-drilled for a single-hole or center-set faucet. Verifying hole spacing and supply clearances in advance prevents costly top replacements.

How to Compare Your Options
Check whether your shower requires a new behind-the-wall pressure-balancing valve or just a trim plate, verify rough-in depth, and review finish durability against hard water mineral buildup.
